study type: Qualitative study (focus group discussions and individual interview)
exposure: Implementation of resuscitation and stabilization with an intact umbilical cord during emergency caesarean sections
outcome: Suggested solutions to common concerns (sterility, temperature control, equipment availability)
Factors for successful implementation (multidisciplinary team, decision-making authority)
cohort: Participants were members of implementation teams responsible for implementing resuscitation and stabilization with an intact cord during caesarean sections from two hospitals in Sweden.
finding: The study identified lessons across all implementation domains except the outer setting, highlighting suggested solutions to common concerns and emphasizing the importance of a multidisciplinary team with decision-making authority for successful implementation.
